preamble: Raising of /æ/ all the way to /i/ is a rare, morphophonological process. Its clearest case is Uyghur 'vowel reduction', in which the low vowels /ɑ æ/ are raised to [i] in word-medial open syllables created by suffixation; in rapid speech the raising can even affect word-final vowels across a word boundary. The previous Dhofari Arabic example (intæ > inti) could not be verified and was removed.

examples.note: In rapid speech the word-final dative vowel /æ/ raises to [i] before the following word, extending the word-medial raising rule across the word boundary.

examples.from: stem-final /æ/ in an open medial syllable
examples.note: The regular rule raises /ɑ æ/ to [i] only in derived word-medial open syllables; underived roots such as /mɑqɑlæ/ 'academic article' do not raise.

sources: Mayer, C., McCollum, A., & Eziz, G. (2022). Issues in Uyghur phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 16(12), e12478. https://doi.org/10.1111/lnc3.12478
